Referral Note

Referral from primary care. Mrs. Holloway is a 41-year-old elementary school teacher who reports more than a year of feeling stressed and on edge, with poor sleep, frequent tension headaches and daytime tiredness. She says it is affecting her work and her home life. She has had no psychiatric treatment apart from brief counseling in college. She is otherwise healthy; recent labs were unremarkable. She takes ibuprofen as needed for headaches and melatonin some nights. Please provide a diagnostic assessment and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Well groomed.

Behavior: Cooperative. Fidgets with the sleeve of her cardigan.

Speech: Normal rate and volume; slightly rapid at times.

Mood / Affect: Mood “stressed.” Affect anxious and congruent.

Thought / Perception: Thought process goal-directed; thought content focused on worries. No suicidal or homicidal ideation. No perceptual disturbances.

Cognition / Insight: Alert and oriented. Insight and judgment good.

1. State your primary DSM-5-TR diagnosis and ICD-10-CM diagnosis code.
Explain why this diagnosis best fits the patient's presentation by discussing at least three to four specific clinical findings from the case.
2. Discuss the single most important differential diagnosis.
Explain why this diagnosis was considered and why it was ruled out using evidence from the patient presentation.
3. Present your initial evidence-based treatment recommendations.
Discuss:
  • Appropriate level of care
  • Medication recommendation (or explain why medication is not indicated)
  • Appropriate psychotherapy
  • One patient education point or safety consideration
4. Conclude your presentation by answering the following question.
What additional question, assessment, or diagnostic information would you obtain before finalizing your diagnosis or treatment plan, and why is this information clinically important?
